forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let a, b, r be integers with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0. Define P_{a,b,r}(q) := product_{i=a+1}^{b} ((1 - q^(r+i)) / (1 - q^i)), with empty product equal to 1. Assume that for every positive integer d one has floor((r+b)/d) - floor((r+a)/d) >= floor(b/d) - floor(a/d). Then P_{a,b,r}(q) is a polynomial in Z[q], and every coefficient of P_{a,b,r}(q) is nonnegative.

semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: If the coefficients of a polynomial over the integers are symmetric around degree D and the coefficients in the first half are nonnegative, then every coefficient is nonnegative.
quantifier_order: Fix a polynomial F in the polynomial ring over the integers, with coefficients c_0 through c_D.
For every integer j between 0 and D inclusive, c_j equals c_{D minus j}.
For every integer j between 0 and floor of D divided by 2 inclusive, c_j is nonnegative.
Therefore, for every integer j between 0 and D inclusive, c_j is nonnegative.

payload.statement_nl: Let D be a nonnegative integer, and let F(q) = sum_{j=0}^D c_j q^j be a polynomial in Z[q]. Assume that c_j = c_{D-j} for every integer j with 0 <= j <= D, and assume also that c_j >= 0 for every integer j with 0 <= j <= floor(D/2). Then c_j >= 0 for every integer j with 0 <= j <= D. Equivalently, every coefficient of F(q) is nonnegative.

result_payload.proof_nl:
Let j be any integer with 0 <= j <= D. We will prove that c_j >= 0.

If j <= floor(D/2), then c_j >= 0 by the given hypothesis on the first half of the coefficients.

Now suppose j > floor(D/2). We claim that D - j <= floor(D/2). Indeed, if D - j were also > floor(D/2), then, since j and D-j are integers, we would have j >= floor(D/2) + 1 and D - j >= floor(D/2) + 1. Adding these inequalities gives
D = j + (D-j) >= 2 floor(D/2) + 2.
But 2 floor(D/2) is either D or D-1, so 2 floor(D/2) + 2 > D, a contradiction. Therefore D-j <= floor(D/2). Also D-j >= 0 because j <= D.

Hence 0 <= D-j <= floor(D/2), so by the hypothesis on the first half of the coefficients we get c_{D-j} >= 0. Using the symmetry hypothesis, c_j = c_{D-j}, and therefore c_j >= 0.

Since j was arbitrary, we have proved that c_j >= 0 for every integer j with 0 <= j <= D. Equivalently, every coefficient of F(q) is nonnegative.
result_payload.proof_summary: For any index j between 0 and D, either j lies in the first half, where nonnegativity is assumed, or else D-j must lie in the first half; otherwise both j and D-j would exceed floor(D/2), forcing their sum to exceed D. Then symmetry c_j = c_{D-j} transfers nonnegativity from c_{D-j} to c_j.
